_comment: Niche funders without a call database. Fields: id, name, funder, group, url (shown), check_url (scanned, optional), selector, deadline_patterns (regex with one date group), recurring_deadlines ['MM-DD'], rolling, closed_patterns, no_text_amount (do not read amounts from page text), never_parse_dates, ignore_default_closed, amount{min_eur,max_eur,funding_rate,note}, eligibility, summary, fit_reason, fit (high|medium|low -> score floor), tags, language. Verified 2026-10-02.

funders.name: Zukunftsfonds der Republik Österreich – Projektförderung
funders.rhythm: Rolling – no deadlines; submit ≥ 3 months before project start, board decides in order of receipt

amount.note: per project and year (higher only by unanimous board decision)

funders.eligibility: Any natural or legal person in Austria or abroad – FH research groups eligible
funders.summary: Funds scientific, historical and educational projects on remembrance of National Socialism and other totalitarian regimes, human rights, tolerance and democracy with a link to Austria. Educational and pedagogical formats are explicitly eligible.
funders.fit_reason: History/remembrance and moral-courage games (cf. CATRINA, museum games) for schools fit the pedagogical project strand.

funders.name: Nationalfonds der Republik Österreich – Projektförderung
funders.funder: Nationalfonds der Republik Österreich für Opfer des Nationalsozialismus
funders.rhythm: Board (Kuratorium) submission deadlines every year on 1 February, 1 April and 1 September

amount.note: no fixed maximum published; 1/3 of the 2025–26 budget reserved for the priority topic

funders.eligibility: Institutions and organisations; projects on NS history, remembrance and education
funders.summary: Project funding for remembrance, research and education about National Socialism and its victims. Priority topic 2025/26: countering online disinformation that relativises the Holocaust – digital and educational formats welcome.
funders.fit_reason: Educational games and interactive formats against Holocaust disinformation match the current priority topic directly.

funders.name: Fonds Gesundes Österreich – Projektförderung & Calls
funders.rhythm: Programmes reopen after the 2027 work programme is adopted (expected early Dec 2026); projects ≥ €100k have one fixed date per year (2026: 16 March) – projects < €100k rolling

amount.note: large-project track from €100,000; pure research not funded

funders.eligibility: Legal persons as project lead (FH eligible); health-promotion projects, not pure research
funders.summary: Austria's national health-promotion fund. Funds practical health-promotion projects; the 2026 call focused on psychosocial health of young people in times of increasing digitalisation.
funders.fit_reason: Game-based and digital health-promotion interventions (e.g. VR stress relief, playful wellbeing apps for youth) fit when delivered with a practice partner.

funders.name: OeNB Jubiläumsfonds – Forschungsförderung
funders.rhythm: Two submission windows per year (2026: 26.01.–18.03. and 27.07.–23.09.); next window expected ~late Jan–mid Mar 2027
funders.eligibility: Austrian research institutions; only research relevant to central banking (19 thematic clusters)
funders.summary: The OeNB's anniversary fund supports research projects relevant to monetary policy, financial stability and the economy. Cluster 16 'Finanzbildung und Wirtschaftskompetenz' (financial literacy) is the relevant entry point.
funders.fit_reason: Only via financial-literacy research – e.g. a game-based learning intervention on money, inflation or the euro for schools, with an evaluation design.

funders.name: Theodor Körner Fonds – Förderpreis Wissenschaft & Kunst
funders.rhythm: Every year 1 January – 31 March
funders.eligibility: Individuals only – highest degree ≤ 6 years ago, work in progress (e.g. lab PhD students / junior researchers)
funders.summary: Annual awards for ongoing scientific and artistic work by early-career researchers and artists in Austria, endowed with €5,000 each.
funders.fit_reason: Seed money for junior lab members' ongoing game or XR research projects.

funders.name: AK OÖ Zukunftsfonds „ARBEIT-MENSCHEN-DIGITAL“
funders.rhythm: Several submission rounds per year until end of 2028 (20th round: until 31.10.2026)
funders.eligibility: FHs explicitly eligible; projects must benefit employees in Upper Austria (company or works-council partner), no pure research
funders.summary: The Upper Austrian Chamber of Labour funds projects that help employees cope with digitalisation – training, participation and new digital tools at work.
funders.fit_reason: Serious games and playful training tools for employees of OÖ companies (e.g. AI literacy, safety, logistics like Logistify).

funders.name: Land OÖ Kultur – Förderung wissenschaftlicher Projekte
funders.funder: Land Oberösterreich, Direktion Kultur und Gesellschaft
funders.rhythm: Rolling – online application before project start

amount.note: no fixed maximum; project, staff and pro-rata overhead costs eligible

funders.eligibility: Researchers, associations and institutions based in Upper Austria; project ≥ 50% related to Upper Austria with public results
funders.summary: Upper Austria's culture department funds scholarly projects in the humanities, cultural and regional studies with a clear Upper Austrian focus and publicly accessible results.
funders.fit_reason: Regional history and heritage games or interactive installations (e.g. Pferdeeisenbahn, Linz city games) fit well.

funders.name: Land OÖ – Gedenk- und Erinnerungskultur
funders.funder: Land Oberösterreich, Direktion Kultur und Gesellschaft
funders.rhythm: Rolling – online application before project start
funders.eligibility: Institutions and initiatives in Upper Austria
funders.summary: Funding for remembrance projects in Upper Austria – memorial sites, educational programmes and mediation formats about National Socialism and regional contemporary history.
funders.fit_reason: Digital/game-based mediation for Upper Austrian memorial sites (e.g. Mauthausen region) or school programmes.

funders.name: Tools Competition – EdTech prizes (Learning Engineering)
funders.funder: Learning Engineering Virtual Institute / Tools Competition
funders.rhythm: Annual cycle: Phase I abstracts ~October, Phase II full proposals ~January, winners ~June
funders.eligibility: Worldwide – universities, non-profits and companies (3 of 4 tracks; the postsecondary track is US-only)
funders.summary: International competition funding digital learning tools and the research infrastructure around them (data, evaluation). Three prize tiers by project maturity; tracks for K-12 learning, assessment and AI-supported learning.
funders.fit_reason: Directly fits the lab's educational games and AI-in-classroom work (KIWi, climate games) – a learning game with a research/data component.

funders.name: Epic MegaGrants (Unreal Engine)
funders.rhythm: Submission cycles announced on the page (2026 cycles closed 4 Sep 2026; next expected early 2027)
funders.eligibility: Game developers, creators, educators and degree-granting institutions worldwide
funders.summary: Epic Games funds projects built with Unreal Engine – games, XR, education, research and open-source tools. Grants are non-dilutive; Epic takes no rights.
funders.fit_reason: Unreal-based educational, museum or VR projects (e.g. VR heritage installations) qualify; education and research are explicit categories.

funders.name: Unity for Humanity Grant
funders.rhythm: Annual – opens ~January, closes ~February (2026: closed 20 Feb 2026)
funders.eligibility: Creators using Unity for social impact; universities have won before (non-US public bodies not explicitly ruled out)
funders.summary: Unity's annual grant for real-time 3D projects (games, XR, simulations) with positive social or environmental impact, including education and inclusion.
funders.fit_reason: Social-impact learning games and accessibility projects (e.g. BlindBits, climate games) built in Unity.

funders.name: NLnet – Open Internet Stack / NGI Zero open calls
funders.rhythm: Every two months on the 3rd of odd months
funders.eligibility: Individuals, universities and organisations worldwide; results must be open source
funders.summary: Small, fast grants for open-source internet technology – libraries, tools, protocols, privacy and accessibility software.
funders.fit_reason: Fits only open-source tooling the lab builds (e.g. Spacehuddle, the ZIEGE game editor, accessible web components), not the games themselves.

funders.name: Prix Ars Electronica & S+T+ARTS Prize – Open Call
funders.rhythm: Annual open call from January, deadline ~early March

amount.note: Prix categories up to €10k; S+T+ARTS Prize 2 × €20k

funders.eligibility: Artists, researchers and institutions worldwide
funders.summary: International prize for media art and digital culture from Linz, plus the EU S+T+ARTS prize for innovation at the intersection of science, technology and the arts.
funders.fit_reason: Interactive installations, XR and playful media works (e.g. e-hackbrett, projection-mapping installations) are classic Prix submissions.

funders.name: Jacobs Foundation CIFAR Research Fellowship
funders.rhythm: Annual – opens ~late November, deadline ~early February
funders.eligibility: Early-career researchers (PhD within 10 years) at a host institution worldwide
funders.summary: Fellowships for early-career researchers studying child and youth development and learning, including learning technologies.
funders.fit_reason: A lab postdoc researching the learning effects of games (learning-science framing) could apply with the FH as host.

funders.name: Japan Prize – International Educational Media Competition
funders.rhythm: Annual call for entries ~April–June; games and apps accepted since 2023
funders.eligibility: Producers of educational media worldwide
funders.summary: NHK's international competition for educational media; the digital category accepts educational games and apps.
funders.fit_reason: Visibility and modest prize money for finished educational games (e.g. Klimaspiel, Ecopolis).

funders.name: CEI Know-how Exchange Programme (KEP)
funders.rhythm: Annual call, deadline ~September (2026: 11 Sep)
funders.eligibility: Lead from an EU CEI member (Austria eligible) with a beneficiary partner from a non-EU CEI country (e.g. Western Balkans, Moldova, Ukraine)
funders.summary: Co-funds the transfer of know-how and good practice from EU to non-EU CEI member states, including education and digital transformation.
funders.fit_reason: Transfer of educational-game methods to schools or universities in the Western Balkans or Ukraine.

funders.name: Interreg Alpine Space – small-scale projects
closed_patterns: currently no call for small-scale projects
funders.rhythm: Small-scale project calls announced irregularly; programme winding down until the post-2027 period
funders.eligibility: Organisations in the Alpine Space area (Upper Austria eligible)
funders.summary: Transnational cooperation programme for the Alps; small-scale projects test ideas on climate, environment, governance and innovation.
funders.fit_reason: Climate-education or tourism games for Alpine regions with partners from DE/IT/SI/CH/FR.

funders.name: Erasmus+ KA220-SCH Cooperation Partnerships – School education
funders.funder: European Commission via OeAD (Erasmus+ national agency Austria)
funders.rhythm: One submission round per year in Austria, usually early March (2026: 5 March); the new deadline appears once the 2027 Programme Guide is published (~November)
funders.eligibility: Any organisation active in the field (FHs can lead or partner); min. 2 (KA210) / 3 (KA220) organisations from different programme countries
funders.summary: Transnational projects that develop, transfer or implement innovative practices – e.g. digital learning materials, teacher training, open educational resources. Submitted to the Austrian national agency (not listed on the EU portal).
funders.fit_reason: Classic vehicle for co-developing and piloting educational games with schools and universities across Europe, including teacher-training materials.
